claim: Centro Botín opens Oct-May Tue-Fri 10:00-14:00 and 16:00-20:00, weekends/holidays 10:00-20:00; June-September Tue-Sun 10:00-21:00.
quote: October to May: Tuesday to Friday, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. and from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. From June to September Tuesday to Sunday, from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m.

claim: Centro Botín's spring 2026 programme features ITINERARIOS XXX and Point and Counterpoint until 19 Apr 2026, with Yuko Mohri: Entanglements running 28 Mar - 6 Sep 2026.
quote: ITINERARIOS XXX (from November 15, 2025 to April 19, 2026), Point and counterpoint (from November 15, 2025 to April 19, 2026), and YUKO MOHRI: Entanglements (from March 28, 2026 to September 6, 2026).

claim: General admission to Centro Botín is €9 online (€10 at the box office), with €5/€6 concessions and free entry for under-18s.
quote: General admission price is €9 when purchased online (€10 at the box office). Concession rates (€5 online / €6 at box office) apply to people over 65 years old, students aged 18 to 25, people with disabilities, and large families.

claim: The Magdalena tourist train runs year-round: 10:00-19:00 in summer (continuous) and 10:00-14:00 / 15:30-18:00 in winter, with 56-passenger heated trains every 15-20 minutes.
quote: Summer hours are 10:00 to 19:00 (uninterrupted service) and winter hours are 10:00 to 14:00 and 15:30 to 18:00, with frequency every 15-20 minutes. The trains are accessible with capacity for 56 passengers each.

claim: The Magdalena Palace itself is typically only open for guided interior tours on weekends; gardens of the peninsula are free.
quote: The palace is often only open on weekends. Check schedules before your visit.

claim: The free Mini Zoo on the Magdalena Peninsula keeps seals, sea lions and penguins in seawater pools, with feeding around 1 pm; the park opens 9:00-20:30 (8:00-22:00 in summer).
quote: The public park on Magdalena Peninsula has a free mini-zoo with penguins, seals, sea lions, and ducks... The seal and penguin feeding around 1 PM is recommended for the best viewing opportunities. The park is open in summer from 8am to 10pm, the rest of the year from 9am to 8.30pm. Free access.

claim: El Sardinero is Santander's longest beach at roughly 1,300 m, split into First (historically the smart end) and Second (popular) beaches, with a continuous promenade.
quote: El Sardinero beach is 4,300 feet (1,300 meters) long and 260 feet (80 meters) deep, making it the longest beach in Santander. The First beach is the most iconic, as the nobility and gentry visited it, while the Second beach was historically reserved for the common people.

claim: The Jardines de Piquío, created in 1925 on a rocky promontory between the two Sardinero beaches, contain the Bola del Mundo limestone sphere and the Mesa Zodiacal zodiac stone.
quote: Notable artworks include the Bola del Mundo, a 26-inch limestone sphere representing oceans and continents, and La Mesa Zodiacal, a circular stone with carved animal figures representing the 12 signs of the zodiac.

claim: The Gran Casino del Sardinero, opposite the First beach, is a 1916 Belle Époque building still hosting gaming, a restaurant and exhibition space.
quote: The Gran Casino Sardinero, opposite the First Beach, is a classic example of La Belle Époque architecture and was built in 1916. Currently, it has an exhibition hall, a cafeteria and a banquet hall.

claim: Santander Cathedral is open Mon-Fri 10:00-13:00 and 16:00-19:30, Sat 10:00-13:00 and 16:30-20:00, Sun/holidays 8:00-14:00 and 17:00-20:00; admission €1 adult / €0.50 child.
quote: Monday to Friday: From 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. and from 4:00 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. Saturdays: From 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. and 4:30 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. Sundays and Public Holidays: 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. and 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. Admission Cost: Adults are €1, and children are €0.50

claim: Mercado de la Esperanza occupies a 19th-century cast-iron hall behind the town hall, with fish stalls on the ground floor and butchers, fruit, veg and cheese above.
quote: Housed in a 19th-century cast-iron structure, the bustling Esperanza market is a lively slice of Cantabrian life with shoppers browsing two floors of stalls laden with seafood, meat, cheese, fruit, vegetables, baked goods.

claim: Mercado de la Esperanza trades Monday-Saturday 08:00-14:00, with extended Thursday and Friday afternoon openings 17:00-19:30; closed Sundays.
quote: Mercado de la Esperanza is open from 8 am - 2 pm Monday through Saturday. On Thursdays and Fridays the market is also open from 5 pm until 7:30 pm. It's shut on Sundays.

claim: The Río de la Pila funicular is free, council-run urban transport climbing 78 m with four stops, operating roughly 06:00 to midnight with bicycles permitted.
quote: The funicular is free to use and operates between 6:00 AM and midnight... The funicular covers 78 meters with four stops: Río de la Pila, Calle San Sebastián, Prado San Roque, and the El Regimiento soccer field on Paseo del General Dávila.

claim: From the upper Río de la Pila funicular station on Paseo del General Dávila, visitors gain panoramic views over Santander bay.
quote: The funicular is a popular tourist attraction that provides impressive views of the entire bay from a different perspective and is a must-see stop when visiting Santander.

claim: Centro Botín, the Renzo Piano-designed art centre on the waterfront, has become Santander's signature contemporary cultural draw since opening.
quote: Centro Botín - Visiting Hours, Tickets, History, and Tips
